question: Does ordered-role auxiliary supervision improve transfer to unseen entity pairs compared with parameter- and compute-matched unordered-identity supervision on new graph layouts?

design.generator: generator_gate_v1 balanced distractors and dedicated padding token
design.endpoint: final update only; no unseen-pair-based checkpoint selection

evaluation.primary_model_metric: mean binary role accuracy over all 25 unseen unordered pairs
evaluation.primary_graph_metric: mean across three paired seeds of ordered_roles minus unordered_identities model metric
evaluation.primary_population_estimate: equal-weight mean of the eight graph metrics
evaluation.test: exact two-sided sign-flip test over eight graph-level paired differences, all 256 sign assignments
evaluation.uncertainty: report all eight graph differences and mean +/- t(7,0.975) * sample_SD(graph_differences)/sqrt(8) as a graph-level 95% interval
secondary: weak-pair fraction below 0.8 binary role accuracy

success_rule: At least +0.05 primary mean improvement and exact sign-flip p <= 0.05; mean seen four-choice loss <=0.01 and mean unseen event loss <=0.02 relative to unordered identity control; report all individual degradations.
analysis_unit: graph; pairs, renderings, and seeds are nested measurements, not independent graph replications
no_adaptive_replacement: All eight graph layouts and all three starts remain in the primary analysis even if learning or transfer is poor. Any run failure is documented and rerun only with the same graph, seed, arm, and source version.
scope_limit: Even a positive result is limited to this coded-message, generated-scene architecture and graph distribution; natural-language and pretrained-LLM claims require separate tests.
